newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: GOVERNMENT NOT TO BACK DOWN ON PRIVATISATION.
newsitem.headline: GOVERNMENT NOT TO BACK DOWN ON PRIVATISATION.

text.p: Lithuanian Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius said on Thursday that the government would not back down on its privatisation plans despite a growing chorus of protests from public sector employees.
"The political decision has been made...we will carry out privatisation even if administrators from certain companies object," Vagnorius told Reuters after a news conference.
Vagnorius' government has committed itself to completing the privatisation process started during his first term of office in 1991-1992.
It says it will sell off several key assets in the energy, communications and transportation sectors.
The government's plans have sparked protests from a number of state-run companies, including Lithuania Telecomm.
Daily Lietuvos rytas printed an open letter on Thursday from employees of Lithuania Telecomm's Kaunas branch, expressing opposition to the sale of their company.
Employees at the state-run television transmission centre and a transport firm in the port of Klaipeda have also protested the government's privatisation campaign in recent weeks.
Vagnorius said that in the case of Lithuania Telecomm, he was uncertain if the protest was inspired by management or workers.
"I am not sure that this letter belongs to the workers (of Lithuania Telecomm)," Vagnorius said.
"I think that the workers of telecomm will benefit most from the investment of private capital," he added.
"I have no doubt that the number of jobs will not decrease and salaries will probably increase," he said.
